articles.title: Nintendo Defends Decision to Cut Mario and Yoshi Easter Eggs From The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake
articles.summary: Nintendo has defended its decision to scrub the secret appearance of Mario characters from its The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. Hidden away inside Hyrule Castle, the game's original 1998 version included a wall of portraits that featured Mario, Luigi, Peach, Bowser, and Yoshi artwork…
body: Visit the same area in Nintendo's newly-launched Switch 2 version, however, and all references to the Mushroom Kingdom have been removed. On a similar note, a selection of Zelda: Twilight Princess artwork has also been cut, having been snuck in when Ocarina of Time was re-released on 3DS.
Now, Nintendo has addressed its choice to remove these Easter eggs — and said that what was once a more "carefree" approach within Nintendo to referencing other games has been reconsidered.

"Certainly, at the time, when we put those there, I don't think anybody thought it was too big a deal," legendary Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma told Game Informer. "Maybe there was a more carefree or comfortable approach to that sort of thing.

"But looking at it now... given the overall way that we're creating this world and giving the player that form of expression, if they look up and they think, 'Why is Yoshi there?' We don't want that moment to interrupt their experience of the world in that way. So we're feeling a little bit differently about it this time."
points: Nintendo has defended its decision to scrub the secret appearance of Mario characters from its The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Players Use In-Game Ocarina to Play Everything From Linkin Park, Titanic, and Japanese Supermarket Themes
articles.summary: The much anticipated remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launched on November 5, and one feature has fast become a big hit: the fact that you can now play any tune you like on Link’s ocarina. Now, social media has become awash with players sharing the results.
body: People are tackling tunes from other video game series like Final Fantasy, anime such as Dragon Ball Z, and film scores including Titanic and The Lord of the Rings. Users often put a pun in the post, usually involving Link or Hyrule.

Over on X, @StevenxTCG got Link to play Linkin Park’s ‘In the End’ on the ocarina. The post proved unexpectedly popular, prompting him to follow up with a guide on how to play it yourself. On a more upbeat note, another poster responded with ‘ Macarena of Time,’ their take on the '90s dance craze.

Themes from other games also proved popular. @KOPPE_lunix posted their rendition of the emotional tearjerker ‘To Zanarkand’ from Final Fantasy 10 and also shared some guidance on how to play. Video game lecturer Dr. T. Wade Langer (aka ProfNoctis) posted a duet of Link and Cloud playing Final Fantasy 7’s main theme, adding that “I want music minigames in every game now.” Another popular choice was Kingdom Hearts’ Dearly Beloved.
More recent games also got some love, with players having a go at everything from Death Stranding’s BB’s theme to Kirby Air Riders’ main theme song Starlit Journey.

articles.title: Magic's Best Unofficial Format Is So Big, Burger King Is Running a Tournament
articles.summary: If you think that the Universe Beyond crossover with beloved sci-fi franchise Star Trek is the biggest thing currently going on in the Magic: The Gathering world, think again. On Nov.
body: Announced through Burger King's Italian website, "Burger King Quest: The Great Gathering" will run from Nov. 10 to Nov. 30. Hungry fans can buy a Great Gathering Bundle at any Burger King restaurant for 19.90 euros ($22.20). The bundle includes a menu, choosing between Double Cheese King, Chicken Krispper, and Whopper Plant Based, plus a deck box and 100 sleeves branded with Burger King x Magic graphics. The deck box in particular has sent Magic players into a frenzy, and it's allegedly already sold out, with scalpers selling it online for ridiculous prices.

This is only half of what Burger King and Magic are cooking, pun intended. Also starting on Nov. 10, nine Burger King restaurants throughout Italy will host Magic tournaments. The winners will qualify for a big final showdown held during the Milan Games Week & Cartoomics, on Nov. 27-29. The tournaments will use the Pauper format, an unofficial 60-card constructed format that allows use of almost every card printed at the common rarity throughout the history of Magic.

articles.title: Nintendo Switch 2 Drops to All-Time Low Price of £309 in Early Black Friday Deal
articles.summary: Black Friday is just a couple of weeks away, but one of the most jaw-dropping deals we’ve seen is one for early-bird UK gamers. AliExpress is offering a steep discount on the Nintendo Switch 2 that brings the latest hybrid handheld/home console down to £309.24.
body: Believe it or not, that’s over £100 less than the MSRP (thanks to a price hike in September of this year ), and in many ways, there’s never been a better time to pick one up.

Right off the bat, it’s worth noting that AliExpress’ early Black Friday deal doesn’t get you any games with your console, but with a huge saving, you can snap up plenty of titles alongside it. Plus, if you have an existing Switch game collection, a lot of those games have handy performance patches for free.

To get the lowest price, you can save an additional £50 with voucher code GBD1133, helping bring the price down even further (and save you money for software). This is also an even better deal than we had previously reported (where the console was down to around £336 instead). The only catch is, you need to be a first time shopper at AliExpress in order to qualify for the massive discount.
While the Switch 2 has always been a great console, and a step up from its predecessor in just about every way, 2026 has seen a bunch of great launches that make it easier to recommend.

articles.title: PS5 Hits 100 Million Units Sold Mark 6 Years After Launch — Here's How It Compares to Other PlayStation Consoles
articles.summary: PlayStation 5 has shipped 100 million units, Sony has announced. The milestone comes ahead of the launch of GTA 6, which is expected to boost console sales significantly.
body: Sony Interactive Entertainment describes shipped units as “Cumulative Worldwide Hardware Unit Sales (Sell-in),” which isn’t sell-through to customers, but does give us an idea of how well the PS5 has sold.

PS5 hits 100 million six years after launch. The console released on November 12, 2020, in select countries and November 19, 2020, worldwide, amid the COVID pandemic and lockdowns. Console rival Microsoft launched the Xbox Series X and S at the same time, and does not report sales figures.

How does PS5 compare to other PlayStation consoles? It’s heading towards PS4’s 117 million total (as of June 30, 2022 — the latest data we have from Sony). It had already outsold the PS3’s 87.4 million total (as of March 31, 2017), and the PlayStation Portable’s 76.4 million as of March 31, 2012. It will soon overtake the original PlayStation’s 102.4 million, but is unlikely to surpass the PS2’s huge 160 million sales. Indeed, PS2 remains the best-selling console of all time, just ahead of the Nintendo Switch’s 157.2 million (as of September 30, 2026). Sony failed to disclose sales data for the PlayStation Vita, but it’s safe to say it wouldn’t have appeared high up on this list.

articles.title: VisionQuest’s Post-Credits Scene Official Confirms Another Avenger Returning in Doomsday
articles.summary: VisionQuest completed the story that began in 2020 with WandaVision, bringing things full circle by again using the framing of classic sitcoms as a way to tell a deep story about grief and family. The VisionQuest finale was released on Nov.
body: One scene is closely tied to the plot of VisionQuest, so it might not pay off for a while, but the other one directly ties into Avengers: Doomsday, Marvel’s next big blockbuster, releasing on Dec. 18. Here’s what it all means. This article contains spoilers for the series finale of VisionQuest.

The first post-credits scene shows Ultron (James Spader) holding a computer chip with the name Jocasta on it. AI and nanotechnology scientists Josephine Carrington (T'Nia Miller) and her husband Virgil Horton (Spader) scanned their own consciousnesses to create advanced AI, with Virgil serving as the blueprint for Ultron and Josephine for Jocasta. After Jocasta died of a degenerative hereditary disease, Virgil put her mind in a new synthezoid body but erased her memories of him. Jocasta and Ultron then fell in love.

articles.title: Monster Hunter Wilds' upcoming Ascendance expansion may be getting a beta, some curious Steam backend updates suggest
articles.summary: Monster Hunter Wilds 's first expansion, Ascendance, is set for release sometime next year. But, judging by some very suspect recent changes to the Wilds beta app on Steam, we may be playing some of the new stuff earlier than we thought.
body: On Steam, Capcom quietly updated the Monster Hunter Wilds Beta app to now say Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance Beta test. You can see the change log on SteamDB (via PC Gamer ), which also shows an updated key art - all signs that point towards an impending beta for Ascendance.

Seeing as Ascendance itself doesn't have a release date, beyond a nebulous 2027 target, it's hard to speculate when Capcom plans to release the beta. Sometime early in 2027 would be a good guess, perhaps alongside a release date announcement.

Capcom has shown off Ascendance on multiple occasions, more recently in Sony's September State of Play, where we got to see a number of the expansion's new features. A few days later at Tokyo Game Show, we got a first look at returning Elder Dragon Teostra, which we can hunt in the expansion.

Capcom is keen for Ascendance to deliver the level of challenge Monster Hunter is known for, following feedback that the launch version of Wilds simply lacked that expected level of difficulty. While post-launch updates have certainly raised the level of challenge, Ascendance looks to be the next step up.

articles.title: World of Warcraft: Forever's magical opening week reminds us all about the power of the MMO, and the threat it poses to your free time
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever is a time vampire. Since its release last Wednesday, I have spent 78 hours in Azeroth. Some of that I was AFK, sure. But for many of those hours, I was lost, happily, in the rolling hills and vast planes of Blizzard's MMO - now enhanced, beautified, and given a new social…
body: The original World of Warcraft is so beloved, so influential, that I wasn't convinced Forever could build upon it without cheapening the overall experience; without creating glaring clashes between its new additions and legacy elements that, in some instances, are now over two decades old. And while there's still plenty I haven't seen after 78 hours and 35 levels, I can speak to one truth: WoW Forever is stunning work.

Perhaps it's best to start with WoW: Forever's most obvious changes: its new lighting and weather effects. People love to speak about getting lost in MMOs, being consumed by their digital worlds, but as much as I've enjoyed World of Warcraft in the past, its ageing graphics tech never managed to ensnare me that way. Forever's new visual elements, though, have gone a long way toward pulling me in.

articles.title: In One Scene, Prime Video Officially Rewrites Gandalf’s Mission in Lord of the Rings
articles.summary: By the end of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power season 2, Gandalf (Daniel Weyman) had chosen his name and wizard staff and found a mentor in the enigmatic Tom Bombadil (Rory Kinnear).
body: Tolkien’s wizards aren’t just old men who wield magical power. They are Maiar, primordial spirits who serve the Valar, the divine beings that helped Eru Ilúvatar create the world. Sauron is a fallen Maia who served the rebel Vala Morgoth. The five Istari are Maiar sent in the form of old Men to Middle-earth to stop Sauron. They became known as wizards, and their members include Gandalf, Saruman, and Radagast.

Those are the only three wizards mentioned by name in The Lord of the Rings, but Tolkien’s Unfinished Tales mentions there were two more who were sent to the East: Pallando and Alatar. In season 3, episode 3, it’s revealed that the Dark Wizard is Pallando. He wanted more than to serve the Valar, so he killed Alatar, an act so evil it turned Rhûn into a desert. Pallando clearly has regrets as he’s trying to regrow the Tears of the Valar lilies that used to cover Rhûn. He hopes that he can make the land green again using one of Sauron’s rings.

articles.title: 5 Years Later, Marvel's Greatest Quote About Grief Just Got Even More Devastating
articles.summary: VisionQuest's stunning finale is a full circle moment for one of the most beautiful lines of dialogue in MCU history
body: One of the best lines of dialogue in Marvel Studios history almost didn't happen.

On the set of WandaVision, the cast and crew were preparing to film one of the show's most pivotal scenes: a heartfelt conversation between Wanda Maximoff (Elizabeth Olsen) and Vision (Paul Bettany). After refusing to confront the grief over her dead husband and instead channeling those emotions into a powerful hex that brings him back to life but also transforms an entire town into a series of sitcom spoofs, Wanda finally faces her emotions head-on. The only problem was, they still hadn't nailed one crucial line.
Speaking at a Space Con panel in 2025, Olsen recalled the last-minute script changes.
“Paul was like, ‘I think we really need to figure out this line. I feel like there’s something we’re missing.’ And then he and the showrunner’s assistant really landed on that line,” Olsen said.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake sells in huge numbers, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game
articles.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has been a huge success for Nintendo, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game ever, shifting more than 5.2 million copies in four days.
body: Nintendo announced the sales result this morning in a press release, specifying that the record relates only to Nintendo-published games. But since Nintendo's games are the most popular Switch 2 games, the fastest-selling-ever title presumably holds.

It's an incredible result for a game that's been received with enormous enthusiasm. Christian Donlan awarded The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time five golden stars in Eurogamer's review, saying: "Alongside great judgement and clever tweaks, this astonishing remake has a proper ace up its sleeve." We've also already seen a jump in US Switch 2 sales because of the game's release. So much for not launching in November near GTA 6, eh?

This level of success begs the question of whether Nintendo would consider remaking more beloved old Zelda games - or Nintendo games - to replicate this nostalgia-driven effect. Are there other Zelda games that have the pull of Ocarina of Time that haven't been remade or remastered already in some capacity?

If you're inspired to pick the game up because of this, or already have it, know that we've got a whole proverbial library shelf of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time guides to help you through the game.

articles.title: PlayStation's embattled shooter Fairgames has finally been cancelled, a new report says, as live service push withers away
articles.summary: After years of silence, we finally know the fate of PlayStation's embattled live service game Fairgames. The Haven-developed co-op heist shooter has been cancelled, with the silver lining that the studio is not closing down or laying off staff.
body: According to a new Bloomberg report, the decision to cancel Fairgames was made following the results of a recent playtest. Sony told staff on Tuesday of the playtest's poor reception and of its decision to end development.

"While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," executives Sean Decker and John Doyle reportedly wrote in an email to staff.
"Combined with challenging market conditions in the PvP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."
A PlayStation spokesperson later confirmed that developers at Haven will now support other teams within the PlayStation Studios group, as they continue to "explore new creative opportunities".
points: After years of silence, we finally know the fate of PlayStation's embattled live service game Fairgames.

articles.title: 'We're kind of friendslop': CEO of Jackbox Games sees the link between party games and this new trend but doesn't think it's necessarily 'a negative moniker'
articles.summary: What was the first instance of a friendslop game? Was it REPO? Human: Fall Flat? Or perhaps it was the first time a group of people tried to guess what someone was saying in what we would now call a game of charades?
body: "We're kind of friendslop in a way," CEO of Jackbox Games, Mike Bilder, tells our Ted Litchfield in a recent interview. With senior software engineer Michael Siciliano adding: "We've just been around so much longer than the term that it feels strange to retroactively [claim it]."

Now, I don't think Jackbox Games goes as far back as the 16th-century origins of charades, but it has been around for a while after its rebrand in 2013, with games like Fibbage and Lie Swatter being over a decade old.

"A lot of our games are just casual with a bunch of friends, and you're drawing ridiculous things trying to make each other laugh, and that's a lot of the impetus of those friendslop games," Bilder adds. "So we don't take issue with it, and I don't think it's necessarily a negative moniker in any way. If anything, it's a bit encouraging.

articles.title: Keeping hold of Company of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO says – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"
articles.summary: In the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio. Responsible for lauded RTS series Homeworld, Dawn of War, and Company of Heroes, they also dabbled in other genres with third-person shooter The Outfit and the original Warhammer 40,000: Space…
body: Without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone. Not only did Relic need the ability to make more games in the series that they were known for, but they also needed the income from back catalogue sales a series like Company of Heroes provides.

Dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013. This was in the immediate aftermath of publisher THQ's bankruptcy auction, where studios and franchises were sold off to the highest bidder. While Sega bought the studio, they didn't buy the licenses to everything Relic had created. "The other games that Relic made – Homeworld, Impossible Creatures, The Outfit... formative games in many people's memory – they were all split up, scattered," Dowdeswell says. "I think that was... I won't say a tragedy, but it's unfortunate because Relic is the home of those games. It would have been great for them to stay with the studio."

points: Side Effects Guaranteed is the first chapter of a two-part expansion for The Outer Worlds 2.
A distress signal beckons you and your crew of the Incognito to a derelict ship, where you discover the ship’s crew in suspended animation—infected with something that causes explosive cell death.
The hunt for a cure leads to Elysium Valley, a brand-new region on Eden.
Two Sub Rosa agents have very different plans for it, and the fate of the valley, the crew, and Sub Rosa itself is yours to decide.
